title: Strict Weil data and the Tate datum
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions]), fix the
geometric-Frobenius datum of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]
and a coefficient ring $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. A
*strict geometric-Weil datum* on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ is a
specified isomorphism in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$

$$
\varphi_K:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K,
$$

that is, a Weil structure in the sense of [sk-def-sf-weil-complexes], with
$\operatorname{Fr}_Y=g_{Y,\gamma}$. The
definition is the same for every $\Lambda$: $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ is the
condensed category of [def-sf-setting], and no coefficient case is reduced
to another. Its scheme-Frobenius form is

$$
u_K=\varphi_K\circ\kappa_{Y,K}:L\Phi_Y^*K\longrightarrow K.
$$

The Tate line $\Lambda_Y(1)$ of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] carries its canonical
datum, the twist normalization of
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists],

$$
\tau_1:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(1)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(1),
\quad
\tau_r:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(r)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(r),
$$

on which geometric Frobenius acts by $q^{-1}$ on $\Lambda(1)$ and by
$q^{-r}$ on $\Lambda(r)$. The induced datum on the source of smooth
purity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^{\mathrm{pur}}_{f,K}:
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\bigl(Lf^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)
&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf^*Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d\ }
Lf^*K(d)[2d],
\end{aligned}
$$

and the datum on the exceptional inverse image is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^!_{f,K}:Lg_{X,\gamma}^*Rf^!K
&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,g_{Y,\gamma},K}\ }
Rf^!Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf^!(\varphi_K)\ }Rf^!K,
\end{aligned}
$$

using the smooth pullback exchange of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]
for the first Cartesian square of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius].

statement_change.old_statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions]), fix the
geometric-Frobenius datum of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]
and a coefficient ring $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. A
*strict geometric-Weil datum* on $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ is a
specified isomorphism in the ordinary triangulated category

$$
\varphi_K:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K;
$$

for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ such a datum is a normalized system of
finite-stage data compatible with the reductions, with a coherent realization
in the derived category of actual towers as in
[def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]; the datum includes the isomorphism of
realized towers, rather than only a family of maps in the individual
ordinary derived categories; for $\Lambda=E$ an
object obtained from an $\mathcal O_E$-datum by inverting $\varpi$,
and for
$\Lambda=\Qlb$ a datum over some finite $E/\Ql$,
modulo further finite coefficient extension (as in
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with the
rationalized common-stage
conventions). In every case the forgetful object lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and $\varphi_K$ denotes the resulting typed
isomorphism. At finite level, $\kappa_{Y,K}$ below is exactly the comparison
of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius], with its specified relative-Frobenius
trivialization of [lem-pur-frobenius-trivialization-pullback]. At integral
level form the comparisons on the strict reduction tower of one K-flat
representative $P$ with flat terms, $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y$.
The finite comparison is induced termwise by the same relative-Frobenius
isomorphism of site objects, with the canonical constant-ring identification.
It therefore commutes with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$: on local sections both composites
apply that site identification and reduce the coefficient modulo $\varpi_E^n$.
After restriction to completed coefficients take the functorial derived limit
of this map of actual towers. This defines
$\kappa_{Y,K}:L\Phi_Y^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K$ using
[def-pur-integral-derived-operations, lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined].
The inverse is obtained by the same construction with the inverse finite
comparison. For $E$, use its image under scalar localization
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; for $\Qlb$, use its morphism class over a
common finite coefficient field [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].
The site identification does not change coefficient sections, so the finite
comparisons commute with coefficient extension; the integral scalar comparisons
of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] identify the two pullbacks
after extension. Thus this prescription uses the same common-stage convention
as the datum, without applying the finite-only Frobenius node directly to a
completed or rational coefficient category. Its scheme-Frobenius form is

$$
u_K=\varphi_K\circ\kappa_{Y,K}:L\Phi_Y^*K\longrightarrow K.
$$

For the Tate construction take $Y_0$ to be finite type over $k_0$,
as in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. The separated finite-type
hypotheses for the smooth-purity constructions are specified below.

The Tate line carries its canonical
datum, the twist normalization of
[def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists],

$$
\tau_1:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(1)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(1),
\quad
\tau_r:Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*\Lambda_Y(r)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_Y(r),
$$

whose geometric-Frobenius action on the coefficient line over
$\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $q^{-1}$ on $\Lambda(1)$ and $q^{-r}$ on
$\Lambda(r)$ by [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar]. Here $q$ is a unit at
all four coefficient stages because $\ell\ne p$.

For the smooth-purity formulas below take $X_0,Y_0$ separated and of
finite type over $k_0$. Then their base changes $X,Y$ are separated
finite-type $k$-schemes, as required by the purity-map domain, and the
canonical Tate data above are defined on both $X$ and $Y$. Use the smooth
separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ in the
fixed geometric-Frobenius datum. Use the operations of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].
The induced datum on the source of smooth purity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^{\mathrm{pur}}_{f,K}:
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\bigl(Lf^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)
&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lf^*Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}
Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Lf^*\varphi_K\otimes\tau_d\ }
Lf^*K(d)[2d],
\end{aligned}
$$

The first arrow is the pullback-tensor isomorphism of
[lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], the pullback-composition
identification for $fg_{X,\gamma}=g_{Y,\gamma}f$ of
[lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the shift
identification; at integral level these are formed on the same strict
reduction towers, and at the field stages on their localized/common-stage
images. The second arrow uses the specified $\varphi_K$ and the canonical
Tate datum.

The datum on the exceptional inverse image is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\varphi^!_{f,K}:Lg_{X,\gamma}^*Rf^!K
&\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,g_{Y,\gamma},K}\ }
Rf^!Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K
\xrightarrow{\ Rf^!(\varphi_K)\ }Rf^!K,
\end{aligned}
$$

Here the exchange has the following precisely typed interpretation.
Write $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_T:T\to s$ for $T=X,Y$.
In the first Cartesian square of [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius],
give the upper-left and lower-left schemes the $k$-structures
$a'_T=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)\circ a_T=a_T\circ g_{T,\gamma}$.
Then $g_{T,\gamma}:(T,a'_T)\to(T,a_T)$ and the two vertical copies of
$f$ are $k$-morphisms: $a'_Yf=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)a_Yf=a'_X$.
These twisted schemes are isomorphic over $k$ to the original schemes
by $g_{T,\gamma}$, so they are again separated and finite type; the
vertical map still has the same underlying smooth morphism and relative
dimension. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ apply exactly
[def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] to this square, with $u=g_{X,\gamma}$,
$v=g_{Y,\gamma}$ and $f'$ the left-hand copy of $f$.
The exceptional functors and coefficient categories here refer to the
underlying scheme morphisms and sites, so $Rf'^!$ is denoted $Rf^!$
in the displayed formula. Correspondingly, at every coefficient stage the
purity isomorphism $\gamma_{f'}$ in the exchange is that of the underlying
morphism $f$: the changed $k$-structures alter neither the sites, nor
$Lf^*$, $Rf^!$ and the twists, nor the diagonal of $f$ over $Y$ from which
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] forms it. At the integral and field stages the
same chosen family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality] is used for
$f'$ as for $f$. Thus $\gamma_{f',M}=\gamma_{f,M}$ for every $M$.

At integral coefficients use the same purity composite
$$
 \operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}_{f,g_{Y,\gamma},K}
 =\gamma_{f',Lg_{Y,\gamma}^*K}\circ b_{\square,K}
   \circ(Lg_{X,\gamma}^*\gamma_{f,K})^{-1},
$$
where $b_{\square,K}$ is the pullback, tensor, twist and shift
identification specified in [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], interpreted
with the integral operations. Use the simultaneous natural, coefficient-compatible integral purity
isomorphisms of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], fixed once in the
coefficient-transport conventions, with the coherent realizations supplied
by [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]. The coefficient equations of the former
lemma specify compatibility after every finite field extension, including
identity and successive extension. This formula uses those actual
isomorphisms and does not infer a unique lift from maps in individual
derived categories. At $E$ use the image of this composite under
rationalization, and at $\Qlb$ its common-stage class, with the purity
transports of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity]. The twist identification
in $b$ is [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] and its tensor
comparison is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. In every case the
exchange and $Rf^!(\varphi_K)$ are isomorphisms, so the displayed composite
is a strict datum. At integral level the induced datum includes its
coherent realization: apply the derived strict reduction functor
$\mathcal R_X$ constructed in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] to
each displayed integral isomorphism $\alpha:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$, in
both $\varphi^{\mathrm{pur}}_{f,K}$ and $\varphi^!_{f,K}$.
This functor is formed by reducing a single K-flat representative at all
levels, and takes arrows to arrows in the derived category of actual
coefficient systems. Its value on $\alpha^{-1}$ is inverse to its value on
$\alpha$ by functoriality. Its evaluations are the finite reductions of
$\alpha$ and satisfy the quotient cocycle of the same reduction functor.
Thus the induced integral data retain actual realized-tower isomorphisms,
as required in the opening definition, without lifting an arbitrary
levelwise diagram. No Cartesian base-change assertion for the second,
scheme-Frobenius square is used.
